Prime Minister has always insisted that technology must permeate not only the
last village but reach every single citizen. The 57th GST Council meeting is
underway at Bharat Mandapur, New Delhi. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sita
Raman is chairing the meeting. The GST Council meeting is deliberating on
policy reforms to resolve GSD disputes and improve the flow of input tax credit with
the aim of reducing the time and cost of compliance. Sources in the Finance Ministry
said the government will propose a five-pronged plan for the next set of reforms to the GSD

bottlenecks in the GSD system and reducing the compliance burden, especially for small

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues.
Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasana, the government has been ceaselessly working
towards achieving the goal of a vikasit Bharat by 2047.
Today in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been
and translated into action through the redevelopment of the historic Jaliyawala Bagh Smarak.
As we take the name of Jaliyawala Bagh, the painful and horrific memories of the brutality
by British gumman comes back. It was here in Amritsar on the Basaki day in 1919 when
troops led by Brigadier General Reginald Dyer killed hundreds of innocent people.
They were assembled here to peacefully protest against the Rolitech Jaliyawala Bagh Smarak
which was then constructed in the memory of those martyred was renovated after decades and
dedicated to the nation by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 28 August 2021. Multiple
development initiatives were undertaken at the complex. Elaborate heritage restoration works
carried out in sync with the local architectural style of Punjab. Four museum galleries were
created showcasing the historical value of events that unfolded in Punjab during that
period. A sound and light show started to display the events that happened on that day.
Visitors to the bug from various parts of the country when contacted appreciated the redevelopment.

A case study on the evolution of water governance in Gujarat and India was launched at IIM
Bengaluru yesterday, in the presence of Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation
under Ministry of Jalsakthi Ashokumar Meena. Taking a page from the case study, the Jalsakthi
Secretary Meena spoke on how people's mission backed by strong institutions, steady investment
and Gram Panchayat ownership can quicken transformation.
Addressing media former secretary in the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation
Parameswara Nair spoke of key learning from the case study
including political leadership, public participation and role of
Panchayat as envisioned by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Now, unless you have community management of people's participation
and you devolve management to the lowest appropriate level, the Panchayats, and get real ownership.
It's very difficult to sustain this program. And lastly, the Co-Pay.
And I think that's a hallmark of Chief Minister, Prime Minister's water management and water governance.
Everything is at scale. It was done in Gujarat and it's done nationally.
The nation is celebrating the 94th anniversary of Indian Air Force today.
Air Chief Marshal AP Singh highlighted the Indian Air Force's growing capabilities and
stressed that its true strength lies in its air warriors rather than merely in advanced
equipment and technology.
Addressing on Indian Air Force Day celebrations at Indian Air Base in Ghaziabad, Air Chief
Marshal Singh emphasized the role of air power in protecting national interests and
described the Indian Air Force as the custodian of the skies.
The Indian Air Force, being the custodian of the air power, understands its role and responsibilities
and is always alert, committed and ready to meet any contingency.
We believe that any Air Force can have the most advanced aircraft in the world or most
advanced systems in the world, but its true strength is measured by its operational preparedness,
that is how quickly and confidently it can act whenever the call comes.
The Air Chief Marshal also recalled the IAF's combat operations during Operation Sindhur,
saying the country saw first-hand the destructive power as well as the effective air defence
operations of the Air Force during the operation.
Veteran actor Nanna Patikar passed away at the age of 75 after suffering a severe cardiac
arrest at his residence in Goa this morning.
Patekar, one of India's most acclaimed actors, was known for his performances across Hindi
and Marathi cinema with a career spanning several decades. He earned widespread recognition
for films such as Parinda, Kranti Veer, Aptak Chappan and Welcome.
Prime Minister Modi has said actor Nana Patekar was an outstanding artist who won the hearts
of audiences through various roles. Addressing an event in New Delhi today, Mr. Modi said
Nana Patekar's life was dedicated to the honour, dignity and pride of the tri-colour.
Mr Modi highlighted that through his films he strongly criticised the prevailing social
system and worked against social evils.
The Prime Minister said Nana Patekar was a strong advocate of taking firm action against
anti-national elements.
The famous actor Nana Patekarji is no longer among us.
He was a great artist who won the hearts of the viewers
through different characters.
Nana Patekarji's life was yearning for the glory and glory of Tirangai.
He was not in a bind.

Vishwanath Partaker, popularly known as Nana Partaker, was born on January 1, 1951 in Murud,
Zanjira in Maharashtra.
Nana was known for its intense performances, distinctive dialogue,
Octology in portrayal of complex characters.
A recipient of three National Film Awards, he was acclaimed for films including Parinda,
Kranti Veer, Agni Sakshi, Natta Samarath, Abhak Chappan and Yashwan.
He made his Bollywood debut with Gaman in 1978 and went on to deliver notable performances
in Shakti, the power of Haran, taxi number 9211 and Rajnithi.
He gained widespread popularity as gangster Udeshatti in Welcome and reprised the role
in Welcome Back.
He remained active in cinema until his final years appearing in House Pull 5, O Romeo and
Subedar, which was released recently.
Pratna Akashwani, News, Mumbai.
India has accused Pakistan of double-speak on terrorism, saying Islamabad is attempting
to gloss over its support for terror groups by announcing a reward for information
on Jaish-e-Mohammad chief Masood Azhar. India said the world has not forgotten the 9-11,
26-11 and Pahal-Ghama attacks. Exercising its right of reply in the UN General Assembly,
India's first Secretary Raghu Puri said terrorism cannot be defeated through declarations and
called for action against its perpetrators, financiers and sponsors.
The Inter-Metrological Department, IMD, has forecast heavy rainfall conditions over
Kerala, Mahadeva, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karayakal, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and Sikkim during
the day.
Now, before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi says government to connect 25 crore students through digital
and online education programs, 5G connectivity reaches every district with over 550,000
base stations, GST Council deliberates on policy reforms to resolve disputes and
improve input tax credit flow. Supreme Court directs center to form committee to curb unethical
pharma marketing practices. Veteran actor Nana Patekar passes away.
India accuses Pakistan of double-speak on terrorism, says Islamabad cannot gloss over

With that, we end the midday news.
